title: Imagined Emotion Study
description: High-density EEG recorded from resting, eyes-closed participants who used voice-guided imagery to enter 15 distinct emotional states, including positive states such as joy and negative states such as sadness and anger. Participants pressed a button when they began to feel the target emotion and again when the feeling waned, with relaxation instructions between the imagery periods. The dataset supports research on EEG-based emotion recognition and brain state dynamics during emotion imagination.
methods_description: Participants listened to 15 voice recordings, each prompting imagination of a scenario evoking a target emotion, and pressed a handheld button at the onset and end of the felt emotion. Relaxation suggestions were played before and between the emotion periods. Raw data were preprocessed to fix event codes and remove excessively noisy channels, then high-pass filtered at 1 Hz for ICA decomposition.
